glossary.Anal canal: The last 3 to 4 cm of the gut, between the rectum and the anus.
glossary.Rectal bleeding: Blood passed from the back passage.
glossary.Anal spasms: Painful involuntary tightening of the anal sphincter muscles.
glossary.Chronic fissure: A fissure lasting more than a week, often with a sentinel tag.
glossary.Off-midline: Not in the front or back midline of the anus, which suggests an underlying disease.
glossary.Red flag: A feature that suggests a serious underlying cause needing urgent action.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination alone, without tests.
glossary.Lateral fissure: A fissure at the side of the anus, such as 3 o'clock, needing investigation.
glossary.Gastroenterology: The hospital specialty dealing with the gut and liver.
glossary.Colorectal: Relating to the colon and rectum.
glossary.Dietary fibre: Indigestible plant material that bulks and softens stool.
glossary.Stool softeners: Laxatives that make stool softer and easier to pass.
glossary.Lubricant: A gel applied before opening the bowels to ease passage of stool.
glossary.Topical anaesthetic: Numbing cream applied to the skin, such as lidocaine.
glossary.Topical steroids: Steroid creams; avoided in fissures because they thin the skin and delay healing.
glossary.Ointment: A greasy preparation applied to the skin.
glossary.Anal sphincter: Ring of muscle that keeps the anus closed.
glossary.Botox: Short name for botulinum toxin, injected to temporarily weaken the sphincter.
glossary.Sphincterotomy: Surgical cut of part of a sphincter muscle to reduce its tone.
glossary.Conservative management: Non-surgical treatment such as diet, laxatives and creams.
glossary.Sphincter tone: The resting tightness of the sphincter muscle.
glossary.Vicious cycle: A loop where each step makes the next worse, so the problem keeps itself going.
glossary.CCB: Calcium channel blocker, such as diltiazem or nifedipine, which relaxes smooth muscle.
glossary.NO donor: A drug such as GTN that releases nitric oxide to relax smooth muscle.
glossary.Smooth muscle: Involuntary muscle, as in the internal anal sphincter and blood vessels.
glossary.Mechanical trauma: Physical injury, here from passing a hard stool.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue.
